input.question: Does eating dirt as a child have any proven benefits for your immune system?
input.ground_truth: Not so much a boosted immune system, but polio affected the upper and middle class far worse than the lower class because kids were exposed to the virus early on in low income areas. As a consequence they became immune to it, while the upper class kids were exposed later in life when it had a far more deleterious effect. [source](_URL_0_)

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Does eating dirt as a child have any proven benefits for your immune system?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you are five years old!

Sometimes, kids might want to eat a little bit of dirt. But doctors and scientists say that eating dirt is **not good** for your body. It can make you sick because dirt can have germs and yucky things that can hurt you.

Some people think that eating a tiny bit of dirt when you are little might help your body learn how to fight germs. But scientists have not found any real proof that eating dirt makes your immune system (that’s the part of your body that keeps you healthy) stronger.

So, it’s better to **not eat dirt**. Instead, you can play outside and let your body meet different things in a safe way, like touching grass or playing with toys. That helps your immune system learn and get strong the right way!
